Fixture: 30_icc_gray_32x32_lossless.jxl (+ 30_icc_gray_32x32_lossless.icc)
32x32 greyscale, mathematically lossless, with a hand-built greyscale
ICC profile -- the E.4.3 header-prediction mismatch case

Purpose
-------
Targets slice 4 (18181-1 E.4, the compressed ICC representation). The
profile is a minimal ICC v2 greyscale display profile: desc, wtpt, kTRC
(a single-gamma curveType) and cprt, 336 bytes in total.

Two things make it worth having. First, E.4.3 predicts the bytes at
offset 12 as "mntrRGB XYZ ", so a GRAY profile forces nonzero residuals
exactly there -- a decoder that hardcoded the predicted string instead of
adding the residual would produce "RGB " and fail here alone. Second,
E.2 requires colour_space to be kGrey when the embedded profile is
greyscale, so this is also the one-colour-channel path through the
want_icc wiring in decode().

Profile structure: header 128 B, tag count + 4-entry tag table, then the
four payloads. Small enough that the whole E.4.5 main content is a
handful of commands.

Provenance

Verification
------------
tools/make-icc-fixtures.sh checks two things on every run, and refuses to
write the fixture if either fails:

  * djxl --orig_icc_out returns a profile byte-identical to the one cjxl was
    given, so the reference really is what the codestream stores;
  * djxl decodes the pixels to a PNM byte-identical to the source, so the
    stream is mathematically lossless.

tests/e2e_icc.rs then asserts that JPXL's own E.4 decoder reproduces the
reference byte for byte, and repeats the comparison against a live djxl when
one is installed.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
